title: It sounds unfair at first.
paragraphs: God hardens a man’s heart… and then punishes him for it?

Sometimes it says Pharaoh hardened his own heart (Exodus 8:15, 8:32).
Other times it says God hardened Pharaoh’s heart (Exodus 9:12, 10:20).
Pharaoh wasn’t a neutral man being forced into evil.
He was already proud. Already cruel. Already enslaving God’s people without mercy.
God doesn’t create evil in Pharaoh’s heart.
He gives Pharaoh over to what Pharaoh already wants.
This is not God playing games.

God is saying:
“You want to resist Me? I will let you feel the full weight of that choice.”
Romans 1 echoes it: God “gave them over…”
But don’t miss the deeper fire here.
God had a purpose beyond Pharaoh.

Exodus 9:16:
“I raised you up for this very purpose, that I might show My power… and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”
Even rebellion becomes a stage for God’s glory.
Even stubborn hearts can’t stop His plan.
And here’s where it hits us.

Ignoring conviction.
Delaying obedience.
Justifying sin.
Little no’s… that become a lifestyle.
Jesus stepped into history not to harden hearts—
At the cross, we see the opposite of Pharaoh.
If Pharaoh shows us the danger of a hardened heart…
Jesus shows us the power of a surrendered one.
And today, you still have a choice.
If this stirred something in you, don’t ignore it.
Come back to Christ while your heart can still feel His voice.
They either soften… or they harden.
